title: Illyrian Kingdom
capsule: The Illyrian Kingdom refers primarily to the Ardiaean state on the eastern Adriatic coast — centered near modern Montenegro and northern Albania — that reached its apex under Agron (died c. 230 BCE) and his widow Teuta, who commanded the largest Illyrian naval force yet assembled and raided as far as Epirus and Acarnania. Teuta's attacks on Roman and Italian merchants precipitated the First Illyrian War (229–228 BCE), after which Rome forced a treaty confining Illyrian activity north of Lissus. Rome fought two further wars against successive Illyrian rulers; in the Third Illyrian War of 168 BCE, the last king Gentius was defeated and captured, and his kingdom dissolved into Roman protectorates. The earlier Dardanian kingdom of Bardylis, operating further inland near Lake Ohrid and defeated by Philip II of Macedon in 358 BCE, represents a distinct though related Illyrian polity.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Ardiaean kingdom's core territory is reasonably attested through Greek and Roman sources and archaeology, but the extent of Illyrian hegemony over neighboring tribes at any given moment is difficult to map with precision.
